candidates.phrase: God as Father reigns with providential care over His universe, His creatures
candidates.rationale: The standard, under a section titled 'God the Father,' directly predicates Father of God as sovereign ruler, asserting divine paternity/relational identity of God Himself.
candidates.chunk_text: God as Father reigns with providential care over His universe, His creatures, and the flow of the stream of human history according to the purposes of His grace. He is all powerful, all knowing, all loving, and all wise. God is Father in truth to those who become children of God through faith in Jesus Christ. He is fatherly in His attitude toward all men. Genesis 1:1; 2:7; Exodus 3:14; 6:2-3; 15:11ff.; 20:1ff.; Leviticus 22:2; Deuteronomy 6:4; 32:6; 1 Chronicles 29:10; Psalm 19:1-3; Isaiah 43:3,15; 64:8; Jeremiah 10:10; 17:13; Matthew 6:9ff.; 7:11; 23:9; 28:19; Mark 1:9-11; John 4:24; 5:26; 14:6-13; 17:1-8; Acts 1:7; Romans 8:14-15; 1 Corinthians 8:6; Galatians 4:6; Ephesians 4:6; Colossians 1:15; 1 Timothy 1:17; Hebrews 11:6; 12:9; 1 Peter 1:17; 1 John 5:7.

candidates.locator: Chapter 2 (Of God and the Holy Trinity), paragraph 3
candidates.phrase: there are three subsistences, the Father, the Word or Son, and Holy Spirit
candidates.rationale: The confession asserts Father as one of three co-equal subsistences of the one God, naming a distinct relational identity within the Godhead.
candidates.chunk_text: In this divine and infinite Being there are three subsistences, the Father, the Word or Son, and Holy Spirit, of one substance, power, and eternity, each having the whole divine essence, yet the essence undivided: the Father is of none, neither begotten nor proceeding; the Son is eternally begotten of the Father; the Holy Spirit proceeding from the Father and the Son; all infinite, without beginning, therefore but one God, who is not to be divided in nature and being, but distinguished by several peculiar relative properties and personal relations; which doctrine of the Trinity is the foundation of all our communion with God, and comfortable dependence on Him. 1 John 5:7; Matt. 28:19; 2 Cor. 13:14 Exod. 3:14; John 14:11; I Cor. 8:6 John 1:14,18 John 15:26; Gal. 4:6

candidates.phrase: The eternal triune God reveals Himself to us as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit
candidates.rationale: The standard asserts that God Himself is revealed as Father among the triune persons, affirming divine paternity/relational identity of God.
candidates.chunk_text: There is one and only one living and true God. He is an intelligent, spiritual, and personal Being, the Creator, Redeemer, Preserver, and Ruler of the universe. God is infinite in holiness and all other perfections. God is all powerful and all knowing; and His perfect knowledge extends to all things, past, present, and future, including the future decisions of His free creatures. To Him we owe the highest love, reverence, and obedience. The eternal triune God reveals Himself to us as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, with distinct personal attributes, but without division of nature, essence, or being.
